meta.game: Twilight Imperium Fourth Edition, base game only (no Prophecy of Kings, no Codex errata)
meta.purpose: Mecatol Online data: base-game technology tree and unit stat lines

counts.note: The base game has 4 general technologies per colour (16 total) plus 9 unit upgrades = 25 cards in each player's technology deck (LRR v1.1 setup step 4: '25 technology cards' per colour set) plus 2 faction techs. '6 per colour / 24 general' is the Prophecy of Kings count; the 8 PoK additions (Dark Energy Tap, Sling Relay, Psychoarchaeology, Bio-Stims, AI Development Algorithm, Self Assembly Routines, Scanlink Drone Network, Predictive Intelligence) are deliberately NOT included.

meta.tier_definition: tier = number of prerequisite symbols on the card (0 = no prerequisites, 3 = three prerequisites of that colour). Within a colour the four general techs form a straight chain: tier 0 needs nothing, tier 1 needs 1 of the colour, tier 2 needs 2, tier 3 needs 3. Owning any tech of a colour satisfies one prerequisite of that colour; unit upgrades have no colour and satisfy nothing (LRR 79.7-79.8). A planet with a technology specialty can be exhausted to ignore one matching prerequisite (LRR 79.14).
meta.research_rules_short: Technology strategy card (initiative 7): primary = research 1 tech, then may spend 6 resources to research 1 more; secondary = spend 1 strategy token + 4 resources to research 1 tech (LRR 80).
meta.two_player_note_disclaimer: 'two_player_note' fields are community-consensus opinion (r/twilightimperium, Space Cats Peace Turtles tier discussions, AsyncTI4 stats), not rules. TI4 base game officially supports 3 to 6 players; 2-player is a house variant.

Fantasy Flight Games, Twilight Imperium Fourth Edition Living Rules Reference v1.1 (02/03/18), sections 79 Technology, 80 Technology (Strategy Card), 86 Unit Upgrades, errata Hyper Metabolism, FAQ Plasma Scoring
Card texts cross-checked against the printed base-game technology cards (Hyper Metabolism uses the LRR-errata wording).

general_technologies.name: Antimass Deflectors
general_technologies.text:
Your ships can move into and through asteroid fields.
When other players' units use SPACE CANNON against your units, apply -1 to the result of each die roll.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: weak on its own; taken as the cheapest blue prerequisite on the way to Gravity Drive.

general_technologies.name: Gravity Drive
general_technologies.text: After you activate a system, apply +1 to the move value of 1 of your ships during this tactical action.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: strong, near-universal first or second pick; mobility wins tempo on a small 7-hex map.

general_technologies.name: Fleet Logistics
general_technologies.text: During each of your turns of the action phase, you may perform 2 actions instead of 1.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: strong; doubling actions per turn is a big tempo swing in a duel where every turn alternates.

general_technologies.name: Light/Wave Deflector
general_technologies.text: Your ships can move through systems that contain other players' ships.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: niche; rarely worth three blue techs, more relevant on a tiny map where the opponent can block the only lane.

general_technologies.name: Neural Motivator
general_technologies.text: During the status phase, draw 2 action cards instead of 1.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: moderate; good if the duel keeps action cards, otherwise just a green prerequisite.

general_technologies.name: Dacxive Animators
general_technologies.text: After you win a ground combat, you may place 1 infantry from your reinforcements on that planet.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: weak; stepping stone to Hyper Metabolism.

general_technologies.name: Hyper Metabolism
general_technologies.text: During the status phase, gain 3 command tokens instead of 2.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: strong; +1 command token every round compounds over a full game.

general_technologies.name: X-89 Bacterial Weapon
general_technologies.text: ACTION: Exhaust this card and choose 1 planet in a system that contains 1 or more of your ships that have BOMBARDMENT; destroy all infantry on that planet.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: niche but brutal in a duel with dreadnought fleets; costs an action and three green techs. Not stopped by PLANETARY SHIELD (LRR 56.1).

general_technologies.name: Plasma Scoring
general_technologies.text: When 1 or more of your units use BOMBARDMENT or SPACE CANNON, 1 of those units may roll 1 additional die.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: solid early pick for PDS or dreadnought players (Letnev flagship, L1Z1X dreads); one extra die per roll, not per unit (LRR FAQ).

general_technologies.name: Magen Defense Grid
general_technologies.text: You may exhaust this card at the start of a round of ground combat on a planet that contains 1 or more of your units that have PLANETARY SHIELD; your opponent cannot make combat rolls this combat round.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: weak (base-game wording); only matters with PDS on contested planets. Note: units treated as lacking PLANETARY SHIELD (e.g. under a war sun) cannot use it (LRR 56.3).

general_technologies.name: Duranium Armor
general_technologies.text: During each combat round, after you assign hits to your units, repair 1 of your damaged units that did not use SUSTAIN DAMAGE during this combat round.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: good with dreadnought-heavy fleets; notoriously strong for Letnev together with Non-Euclidean Shielding (the LRR FAQ even covers the resulting stalemate).

general_technologies.name: Assault Cannon
general_technologies.text: At the start of a space combat in a system that contains 3 or more of your non-fighter ships, your opponent must destroy 1 of their non-fighter ships.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: strong in a combat-heavy duel; a free kill before dice in every big fight.

general_technologies.name: Sarween Tools
general_technologies.text: When 1 or more of your units use PRODUCTION, reduce the combined cost of the produced units by 1.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: strong; one free resource every production is the best tier-0 economy tech. Only applies to the PRODUCTION ability (LRR FAQ).

general_technologies.name: Graviton Laser System
general_technologies.text: You may exhaust this card before 1 or more of your units uses SPACE CANNON; hits produced by those units must be assigned to non-fighter ships if able.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: moderate for a PDS-turtle plan (pairs with PDS II), otherwise a yellow stepping stone.

general_technologies.name: Transit Diodes
general_technologies.text: You may exhaust this card at the start of your turn during the action phase; remove up to 4 of your ground forces from the game board and place them on 1 or more planets you control.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: niche; occasionally useful to shore up a threatened planet without a carrier.

general_technologies.name: Integrated Economy
general_technologies.text: After you gain control of a planet, you may produce any number of units on that planet that have a combined cost equal to or less than that planet's resource value.
general_technologies.two_player_note: Opinion: moderate late-game value; on a 7-hex map there are few planets left to take by the time you have three yellow techs.

unit_upgrades.name: Infantry II
unit_upgrades.text: After this unit is destroyed, roll 1 die. If the result is 6 or greater, place the unit on this card. At the start of your next turn, place each unit that is on this card on a planet you control in your home system.
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: good; better ground combat plus free returning infantry makes planets sticky.

unit_upgrades.name: Fighter II
unit_upgrades.text:
This unit may move without being transported.
Fighters in excess of your ships' capacity count against your fleet pool.
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: strong swarm option; cheap hits and independent movement, but Destroyer II punishes it.

unit_upgrades.name: Destroyer II
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: situational; the counter to a fighter-heavy opponent, otherwise skip.

unit_upgrades.name: Cruiser II
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: strong; move 3 with capacity 1 lets cruisers drop infantry anywhere on a 7-hex map, but the mixed prerequisites are awkward.

unit_upgrades.name: Carrier II
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: strong and common; move 2 plus capacity 6 is the standard invasion engine, and it shares the blue path with Gravity Drive.

unit_upgrades.name: Dreadnought II
unit_upgrades.stat_line: Cost 4, Combat 5, Move 2, Capacity 1, SUSTAIN DAMAGE, BOMBARDMENT 5
unit_upgrades.text: This unit cannot be destroyed by "Direct Hit" action cards.
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: strong for dreadnought factions; L1Z1X uses its own Super Dreadnought II instead (see faction_extras).

unit_upgrades.name: PDS II
unit_upgrades.text: You may use this unit's SPACE CANNON against ships that are adjacent to this unit's system.
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: strong on a 7-hex map: adjacent-range space cannon covers most of the board (works through wormholes, LRR 89.2), and structures are free via Construction.

unit_upgrades.name: Space Dock II
unit_upgrades.stat_line: PRODUCTION X (X = planet resource value + 4); up to 3 fighters in system do not count against capacity
unit_upgrades.text:
PRODUCTION X
This unit's PRODUCTION value is equal to 4 more than the resource value of this planet.
Up to 3 fighters in this system do not count against your ships' capacity.
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: moderate; only matters when the production cap (resources+2) is what limits you, which happens with rich home planets like [0.0.0] (5) or Arc Prime (4).

unit_upgrades.name: War Sun
unit_upgrades.stat_line: Cost 12, Combat 3 (x3), Move 2, Capacity 6, SUSTAIN DAMAGE, BOMBARDMENT 3 (x3)
unit_upgrades.text: Other players' units in this system lose PLANETARY SHIELD.
unit_upgrades.two_player_note: Opinion: late-game finisher; 12 resources and four techs is a long road, but in a duel one war sun often decides the Mecatol fight. Note: there is no 'War Sun I' on the faction sheet; the tech unlocks the unit (Muaat excepted).

base_units.name: Fighter
base_units.stat_line: Cost 1 (x2), Combat 9 (no move value: must be transported; counts against capacity, not fleet pool)

base_units.name: Dreadnought
base_units.stat_line: Cost 4, Combat 5, Move 1, Capacity 1, SUSTAIN DAMAGE, BOMBARDMENT 5

base_units.name: War Sun
base_units.stat_line: Cost 12, Combat 3 (x3), Move 2, Capacity 6, SUSTAIN DAMAGE, BOMBARDMENT 3 (x3); other players' units in this system lose PLANETARY SHIELD (requires War Sun technology)

base_units.name: PDS
base_units.stat_line: PLANETARY SHIELD, SPACE CANNON 6 (placed via Construction; max 2 per planet)

base_units.name: Space Dock
base_units.stat_line: PRODUCTION X (X = planet resource value + 2); up to 3 fighters in this system do not count against your ships' capacity (placed via Construction; max 1 per planet)

base_units.name: Flagship (faction specific)
base_units.note: Each faction has a unique flagship; see faction_extras for the two duel factions.

faction_extras.note: Bonus data for the two factions of the first Mecatol Online version (not general technologies).

faction_technologies.name: Super Dreadnought II
faction_technologies.stat_line: Cost 4, Combat 4, Move 2, Capacity 2, SUSTAIN DAMAGE, BOMBARDMENT 4
faction_technologies.text: This unit cannot be destroyed by "Direct Hit" action cards.

faction_technologies.name: Inheritance Systems

faction_units.name: Super Dreadnought I
faction_units.stat_line: Cost 4, Combat 5, Move 1, Capacity 2, SUSTAIN DAMAGE, BOMBARDMENT 5
Cost 8, Combat 5 (x2), Move 1, Capacity 5, SUSTAIN DAMAGE
faction_units.text: During a space combat, hits produced by this ship and by your dreadnoughts in this system must be assigned to non-fighter ships if able.

faction_technologies.name: L4 Disruptors

faction_technologies.name: Non-Euclidean Shielding

faction_units.name: Arc Secundus

At the start of each space combat round, repair this ship.

results.general_technologies: All 16 confirmed: names, colours and prerequisite counts match TTPG technology.data.js exactly (tier 0/1/2/3 chain per colour); card texts match ti-assistant base texts (Magen Defense Grid and X-89 Bacterial Weapon use the pre-Codex base wording, the Omega/Codex texts are different and correctly absent).
results.unit_upgrades: All 9 confirmed: prerequisites match TTPG (Infantry II GG, Fighter II BG, Destroyer II RR, Cruiser II GYR, Carrier II BB, Dreadnought II BBY, PDS II RY, Space Dock II YY, War Sun RRRY); stat lines match TTPG unit-attrs and ti4calc; texts match ti-assistant.
results.base_units: All stat lines confirmed against TTPG unit-attrs (incl. carrier move 1 / capacity 4, dreadnought move 1, destroyer AFB 9 x2, PDS space cannon 6, space dock production resources+2, flagship cost 8).
results.faction_extras: Super-Dreadnought I (capacity 2) and II (combat 4, bombardment 4, move 2, capacity 2, BBY), Inheritance Systems (YY), [0.0.1] (combat 5 x2, capacity 5), L4 Disruptors (Y), Non-Euclidean Shielding (RR), Arc Secundus (combat 5 x2, bombardment 5 x3, capacity 3, loses-planetary-shield) all confirmed against TTPG, ti-assistant and ti4calc.
results.pok_leakage: None. The 8 PoK general technologies and PoK unit data are present in the TTPG source with source=PoK and are absent here.
results.premise_check: The reviewer brief claimed the base game has exactly 24 general technologies. That is wrong: LRR v1.1 setup step 4 gives 25 technology cards per colour set, which is 16 general (4 per colour) + 9 unit upgrades; TTPG lists exactly these 25 base cards. 24 general (6 per colour) is the Prophecy of Kings count. The meta.counts note in this file was already correct and is kept.

corrections_applied: Removed the 'subtitle' field from all 9 unit upgrades (Gen Synthesis, Advanced Fighters, Automated Defense Turrets, Stasis Capsules, XRD Transporters, Type IV Drive, Deep Space Cannon, Enviro Compensator, Mobile Base). These were Twilight Imperium 3rd Edition technology names ('Mobile Base' matches nothing at all); no TI4 data source (AsyncTI4, TTPG lang/en.json, ti-assistant) carries any subtitle for unit upgrade cards. 'Deep Space Cannon' is kept on PDS II as 'lrr_alias' only, because LRR v1.1 section 66 and 89.2 refer to the card as 'PDS II - Deep Space Cannon'.
unresolved: Dreadnought II / Super-Dreadnought II text: this file and AsyncTI4 read 'This unit cannot be destroyed by "Direct Hit" action cards.'; ti-assistant paraphrases it as '"Direct Hit" cards are no longer effective against this type of ship.' No card scan could be fetched (fandom wiki and BoardGameGeek are Cloudflare-blocked); the AsyncTI4 wording is kept.
Whether the printed unit upgrade cards carry any subtitle could not be verified from a card scan for the same reason; all machine-readable TI4 sources agree there is none.
